rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil (2X Long WTI)
positions.catalyst: The US-Iran war is the freshest and most live catalyst on the tape. US Central Command confirmed overnight it completed a SIXTH consecutive night of strikes on Iran, hitting military logistics and maritime capabilities; Tehran has vowed to target regional energy infrastructure if Trump follows through on threats against its key facilities. Last month's truce has fractured and flows through the Strait of Hormuz — ~20% of the world's seaborne oil — are disrupted again. Brent Sep +0.9% to $85.01, WTI Aug +1.0% to $79.74; both contracts are +11% on the week, their best week since late April. UCO live 40.18x40.23 (Robinhood pre-market 11:42Z), +2.8% vs the 39.15 close — well inside the no-chase band. Equity tape is separately risk-off (QQQ -1.5%, SMH -2.7%, MU -1.7%, WDC -3.0% pre-market), which UCO is deliberately insulated from.
positions.driver: Long crude via a 2x PURE-COMMODITY vehicle — not an energy-equity fund — so there is no equity beta on a day the Nasdaq is gapping down 1.5%. The payoff is genuinely asymmetric: an actual Hormuz closure or a strike on Gulf infrastructure is a +15-25% crude event (UCO +30-50%), while the bear case is a ceasefire headline into a war premium that has a hard floor — and a truce that JUST fractured is unlikely to be re-cut within 24h. Friday adds a well-documented tailwind: traders bid crude into the weekend for gap protection when a shooting war is active. 2x (not 3x) matches conviction: the catalyst is strong and fresh, but crude is already +11% on the week so some premium is priced. RUNNERS-UP: SQQQ (3x inverse Nasdaq) — yesterday's winner and thematically still right, but rejected as a crowded short on DAY FOUR of the same memory rout with the gap already made (+4.7% pre-market), on monthly opex Friday, while UBS/BofA publish 'healthy reset, buy the dip' notes; risk/reward there is now symmetric at best. SOXS (3x inverse semis) rejected as a chase at +8.8%, inside the no-chase band. SOXL (3x long semis) rejected — falling knife, -8.5% pre-market. UVXY rejected at +7.5% with structural roll decay. GUSH/ERX (2x energy equities) rejected — right theme, wrong vehicle: equity beta drags them down with the tape, and ERX is showing a $1.77-wide pre-market spread. USO (1x crude) was the safer expression but leaves too much upside on the table given the conviction.
positions.risks: Primary risk is a de-escalation or ceasefire headline — crude has run +11% in a week, so the war premium is fat and unwinds violently; at 2x, an -8% crude day is -16% here. Secondary: Trump has repeatedly disputed that Hormuz is actually closed, and any 'the strait remains open to commercial traffic' statement takes the tail premium out fast. Third: a broad risk-off in which crude gets sold as a growth/demand proxy alongside equities, or an OPEC+/SPR supply response. UCO also carries 2x daily-reset decay if crude chops sideways. Hard stop 37.01 (-8% on the 2x, ~ -4% WTI) only trips on genuine de-escalation, not intraday chop.
